title: Accuracy of predictive equations for resting metabolic rate: a systematic review
content: Systematic review of predictive resting-metabolic-rate equations against measured (indirect calorimetry) RMR — across studies, Mifflin-St Jeor is consistently among the more accurate widely-used equations for general adult populations on average, but individual-level prediction error is still commonly in the range of roughly ±10-15% (sometimes more) for any single person — population-average accuracy does not guarantee individual accuracy.

title: Accuracy of predictive equations for resting metabolic rate: a systematic review
content: RMR equation accuracy review — Product implication: any Mifflin-St Jeor-based calorie estimate in this app must be presented as a starting ESTIMATE with an explicit uncertainty range, never as an exact number, and should be refined over 2-4 weeks using the individual's own observed weight-trend and logged intake data rather than trusted as precise on day one — this is exactly why nutrition_calculator.ts's output carries a `confidence` field and this codebase's Phase 2 adaptive-nutrition engine exists to recalibrate from real trend data.
